title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Explore the unique rituals and symbols of the first college chartered in the newly recognized United States, from mermaid lore to the sacred steps of Old West.

cards.title: The Convocation Ascent
cards.subtitle: Old West
cards.notes: Walk up the historic limestone steps of Old West during Convocation to ceremonially sign into the college as a first-year student.
cards.short_summary: First-year students ascend the Old West steps during Convocation to sign the college's matriculation book.
cards.evidence_claim: During Convocation, new students walk up the steps, through the doors into Memorial Hall and sign into the college.
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during the Convocation ceremony in August.

cards.title: The Commencement Descent
cards.subtitle: Old West
cards.notes: Exit through the doors of Old West and descend the stone steps as a graduate, a tradition held since 1967.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors descend the Old West steps during Commencement to symbolize their transition to alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: At Commencement, the graduating class walks out the doors and down the steps, symbolically exiting the college.
cards.source_title: Old West Then and Now | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during the Commencement ceremony in May.

cards.title: The Unexpected Mermaid
cards.subtitle: Old West Cupola
cards.notes: Look for the mermaid atop Old West, a coppersmith's 1803 mistake that became the college's most beloved symbol.
cards.short_summary: A mermaid weathervane, originally intended to be Triton, serves as a primary symbol of Dickinson College.
cards.evidence_claim: The local metalworker created a mermaid instead of the requested Triton; the original is now in the library while a replica is on Old West.
cards.source_title: The Mermaid Story | Archives & Special Collections - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: The replica is visible atop Old West; the original is displayed in the Waidner-Spahr Library.

cards.title: Don't Step on the Seal
cards.subtitle: Britton Plaza
cards.notes: Avoid treading on the bronze college seal embedded in Britton Plaza to ensure you graduate on time.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition warns that stepping on the college seal in Britton Plaza prevents graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: Legend has it that if a student treads on the college seal embedded in the middle of Britton Plaza, he or she won't graduate.
cards.access_notes: The seal is located outdoors in the center of Britton Plaza.

cards.title: The Cafsgiving Feast
cards.subtitle: Holland Union Building
cards.notes: Join the campus community for a Thanksgiving meal served by college administrators and staff in the dining hall.
cards.short_summary: Cafsgiving is an annual communal Thanksgiving dinner where staff serve students.
cards.evidence_claim: Every year, the campus community gathers for Cafsgiving, a communal Thanksgiving meal served by college staff and administrators.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in November before Thanksgiving break.

cards.title: Charter Day Celebration
cards.subtitle: Old West Lawn
cards.notes: Celebrate the 1783 signing of the college charter with an annual picnic and philanthropy events on September 9.
cards.short_summary: Charter Day commemorates the founding of Dickinson College with campus-wide festivities.
cards.evidence_claim: Charter Day commemorates the signing of the college's charter in 1783 and celebrates philanthropy at Dickinson.
cards.access_notes: Held annually on or near September 9.

cards.title: The Red Devil's Moxie
cards.subtitle: Biddle Field
cards.notes: Cheer for the Red Devil, a mascot named in 1930 after a sportswriter praised the football team's grit.
cards.short_summary: The Red Devil is the official mascot of Dickinson College, originating from a 1930 football game.
cards.evidence_claim: A Washington writer dubbed the Dickinson team “the Red Devils” in 1930 because of their grit against George Washington University.
cards.source_title: The Dawn of the Red Devil | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Appears at athletic events and campus celebrations.

cards.title: The Tapping Ceremonies
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide
cards.notes: Watch the annual spring tapping ceremonies where students are inducted into honorary societies like Raven's Claw.
cards.short_summary: Dickinson's honorary 'hat societies' tap new members each spring based on leadership and academics.
cards.evidence_claim: Each spring brings members of the community together for tapping ceremonies for honorary societies known as “hat societies.”
cards.access_notes: Ceremonies take place at various campus locations in the spring.

cards.title: Wearing the Red and White
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide
cards.notes: Sport the college colors derived from the 18th-century Belles Lettres and Union Philosophical literary societies.
cards.short_summary: Dickinson's red and white colors originate from its two oldest student literary societies.
cards.evidence_claim: The official red and white colors emerged from the societies' symbols: a red rose for Belles Lettres and a white rose for UPS.
cards.access_notes: Celebrated during 'Wear the Red Fridays' and athletic events.

cards.title: The Global Directional Sign
cards.subtitle: Old West Lawn
cards.notes: Check the signpost in front of Old West that points toward Dickinson's global study centers around the world.
cards.short_summary: A directional signpost highlights Dickinson's commitment to international education.
cards.evidence_claim: The directional sign located in front of Old West shows these global connections by pointing to Dickinson centers around the world.
cards.access_notes: Located on the lawn in front of Old West.
